assessment.nobel_worthiness: Created a systematic, formal and empirical framework for how constitutions, electoral rules, state capacity and political institutions shape fiscal policy and development. It opened a field that is now mainstream across economics and political science. Its influence is broad and conceptually deep, and it is adjacent to the institutions-and-prosperity theme recognised in 2024 without duplicating it.
assessment.attribution: The three are the recognised core of the field through their joint and separate theoretical and empirical work. The monographs by Persson and Tabellini, and the work by Besley and Persson on state capacity, are widely identified with them. Others, such as Acemoglu and Robinson, have already been honoured. Three names fit the topic cleanly.
assessment.maturity: Mature. The key work dates from the 1990s to the 2010s and has been tested, replicated and extended for decades. The field has had time to demonstrate lasting impact.
uncertainties: A possible institutional or personal connection to the committee environment is disclosed but not adjudicated here.
Some of the cross-country empirical results on electoral rules are debated, though the framework is not.
Overlap with the 2024 prize could reduce urgency for some members.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The heterogeneous-firm trade model reoriented trade theory and empirics around firm selection and productivity reallocation. It explains who exports, how trade raises aggregate productivity, and why gains from trade operate through the extensive margin. It has had a large influence on empirical trade and policy analysis.
assessment.attribution: Melitz (2003) is the central contribution, and Helpman, with Melitz and Yeaple, extended it to exports versus FDI. Redding is a leading contributor to the quantitative and spatial extensions but is arguably a step removed from the core discovery. Helpman and Melitz give the cleanest credit.
assessment.maturity: Mature. More than two decades of confirmation, with a large empirical literature supporting the main mechanisms.
uncertainties: Whether the committee prefers to include Redding or other contributors such as Bernard and Jensen (not listed here).
Trade was last recognised in 2008, which may weigh on timing for some members.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Methods for estimating demand and supply in differentiated-product markets (BLP) and for estimating dynamic industry models are the workhorse of empirical industrial organisation, merger analysis and antitrust practice. They are a major methodological advance with direct policy use.
assessment.attribution: The BLP contributions by Berry, Levinsohn and Pakes are well-defined and clearly credited. The wider list (Bresnahan, Reiss, Benkard, Levin) reflects the broader field, but the narrowest core of the discovery is BLP.
assessment.maturity: Mature. Roughly three decades of use across fields, with extensive applied validation.
uncertainties: Choice between honouring BLP alone and a broader empirical-IO recognition that could include Bresnahan.
Methods and structural-estimation prizes can be seen as less central than substantive discoveries.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Reshaped understanding of how technology, trade and tasks change labour demand and wage inequality. It combines credible empirical identification with conceptual framing, and it has strongly influenced both research and policy debate on globalisation and automation.
assessment.attribution: Autor is central across the task approach and the China-shock work. Hanson and Dorn are co-authors of the trade-shock results. Katz is a long-standing figure in the skill-premium literature and also appears on another ballot item, so credit is spread over several contributors. Dorn could also be argued for.
assessment.maturity: Fairly mature. The skill-biased change and task literatures are decades old, and the China-shock results have been replicated and debated for about a decade.
uncertainties: Attribution is split between the task framework and the trade-shock evidence, and a three-person limit forces an uncertain choice.
Some magnitudes and interpretations of the China-shock results remain debated.
Overlap with the 2021 prize recognition of empirical labour methods.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Brought historical tax and distributional data to the study of top incomes and wealth, and changed both research and public debate about long-run inequality. This is a major data and measurement contribution that is highly relevant to political-economy questions.
assessment.attribution: The top-income series are most closely associated with Piketty and Saez. Zucman's contributions on wealth and offshore holdings are important but more recent. Piketty's theoretical claims about r > g are contested, so the strongest case rests on measurement.
assessment.maturity: Moderately mature for the income series (about two decades) and less so for the wealth estimates, which are still debated.
uncertainties: Methodological critiques of the wealth-distribution estimates and of the theoretical claims.
Whether the committee considers measurement and data contributions sufficient without a settled causal theory.
Public prominence is not evidence of scientific merit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Kiyotaki-Moore credit-cycles model showed how collateral constraints amplify and propagate shocks, a foundation for modern macro-finance and the analysis of financial crises. It is conceptually important and of continuing policy relevance.
assessment.attribution: Kiyotaki and Moore have clear joint credit for the 1997 model. Gertler and Gilchrist (financial accelerator) are important, but Bernanke, Gertler and Gilchrist's accelerator overlaps with the 2022 recognition of Bernanke's work.
assessment.maturity: Mature. Nearly thirty years of influence, and the 2008 crisis strongly reinforced its relevance.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2022 prize on banking and financial crises could reduce its marginal appeal.
The line between the Kiyotaki-Moore and Bernanke-Gertler contributions.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Used granular microdata to show that household debt expansions drive credit booms and subsequent busts and weak recoveries. This is an influential empirical contribution to macro-finance and crisis analysis.
assessment.attribution: Mian and Sufi are the unambiguous joint core of the work, and their book and papers are tightly associated with them. Campbell's mortgage and household-finance contributions are distinct and weaker fits to the stated discovery.
assessment.maturity: Moderately mature. The central findings are about 15 years old and still being tested and refined.
uncertainties: Relatively recent compared with other candidates, with some debate on identification and external validity.
Overlap with the 2022 prize on financial crises.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Nominal rigidities, staggered pricing and the New Keynesian framework are the basis of modern monetary policy analysis and central-bank practice. Impact on both theory and policy is very large.
assessment.attribution: Attribution is the main difficulty. Calvo (pricing), Taylor (staggered contracts and the policy rule) and Woodford (synthesis and normative theory) are the clearest individual contributors. Galí, Christiano, Eichenbaum, Evans, Gertler and Smets also made major contributions, and the three-laureate limit leaves out several.
assessment.maturity: Very mature. The core ideas date from the 1980s through the 2000s and have been used widely in practice.
uncertainties: Dispersed credit across many contributors makes any selection contestable.
Overlap with prior macroeconomics prizes on expectations and policy.
Questions about the empirical performance of the framework since the 2008 crisis and in the inflation episode of the 2020s.
